confirmedIssues: REVERIFY-02-001 (new, blocking-candidate; introduced surface touched by fix-batch-001): cascadeTurnDelete omits the pair-counterpart cascade that the impl-lead ruling epic-fix-001 established. The ruling ('the call/result pair is a source dependency; deleting or editing one half is a source change for the counterpart's summary', recorded in team-impl-log.md) was applied to cascadeFromMessage and cascadeMessageDelete but not to cascadeTurnDelete in the same file (packages/lhc/src/domains/messages/internal/cascade.ts:279-306), even though turn delete deletes member messages that can be halves of cross-turn pairs. Dynamically verified end-to-end: batch [user_prompt, tool_call, turn_end] closes t1 with summary outcome 'unknown'; later batch [user_prompt, tool_result(same callId), turn_end] lands the late result in t2 and AC-2.8's intake repair rebuilds the t1 call summary to outcome 'succeeded' at sourceVersion 2 (cross-turn pairing is reachable: intake validation is shape-only and non-transition kinds stamp to whatever turn is open, pipeline.ts:195-198); turns.deleteTurn(t2) then returns cleared:[] — the t1 call summary is never cleared or requeued and remains ready/'succeeded', derived from a record no longer in the readable record (the AC-2.4/AC-6.1 staleness pattern of EPIC-02-BLOCK-002, surviving through the third mutation path that shares DD-8's one cascade module). With BLOCK-002a's read filter in place an explicit requeue now rebuilds 'unknown' correctly, so exposure is narrower than the original blocker, but nothing flags the stale form and the recorded cascade contract is violated. Quick fix: collect pairedCounterpartSubject for each deleted member (skipping counterparts that are themselves members of the deleted turn, deduped) in cascadeTurnDelete, plus a cross-turn regression test.

E02-NB-001 (retained, non-blocking, minor): mutation and requeue operations still bypass the SDK-injected clock — five runInTransaction(db, () => new Date(), ...) sites confirmed at messages/index.ts:331,421,503 and turns/index.ts:356,433. Recorded as deliberately out of fix-batch-001.
E02-NB-003 (retained, non-blocking, observation): the deterministic provider remains the only registered named provider; by design per DD-11 and the epic's scope exclusion of real adapters.
E02-NB-004 (retained, non-blocking, observation): thrown handler errors are still converted to retryable attempts (scheduler.ts:144), documented in place.
E02-NB-005 (retained, non-blocking, observation): attempts accounting asymmetry between terminal paths still present (scheduler.ts:122 vs 162).
result.readinessAssessment: Both canonical blockers are fixed in their ruled scope and the fixes verify independently. EPIC-02-BLOCK-001: per-SDK-instance seam via AsyncLocalStorage (shared/context.ts InstanceSeam/runWithInstanceSeam/resolveInstancePoke; sdk.ts scopeSurface wraps intakeStream/messages/turns/work.drain; enqueue's poke rides ctx.poke) matches the per-instance-scoping ruling; the required regression tests exist and pass (test/epic-fix-02.test.ts, background-then-manual and manual-then-background, manual rows stay queued until explicit drain with a live-background positive control). The module-global slots survive only as a documented below-SDK default for direct non-SDK calls — a recorded deviation from the literal 'replace the slots' wording that cannot auto-drain a manual SDK (every manual sdk.* operation runs in the no-op seam); the unscoped sdk.threads surface is benign (no threads public operation opens a thread database — all openThreadDatabase callers are scoped surfaces or the scheduler). EPIC-02-BLOCK-002a: findPairedBlock and findUnknownOutcomeCallSummary now join message with deleted_at IS NULL; regression test proves a deleted result's call summary rebuilds outcome 'unknown'. EPIC-02-BLOCK-002b: edit and message-delete cascades clear+requeue the live pair counterpart; TC-6.2's cascade-scope assertion was amended per the recorded ruling with the red-manifest hash re-recorded (test-immutability passes); the cascade-scope clarification is recorded in the impl log (fix-batch item 4). Gates re-run independently: pnpm run verify-all exit 0 (build, typecheck, lint 76 files, boundaries, 30 test files / 234 tests including the 3 new regression tests) and pnpm run green-verify exit 0 (27 Red-phase files unchanged). However, the ruling's application is incomplete: cascadeTurnDelete — one of the three mutation close paths sharing the one cascade module — leaves a dynamically-reproduced stale-outcome path (REVERIFY-02-001), so the candidate cannot cleanly close against its own recorded cascade contract. Process notes for closeout: both epic-fix harness envelopes errored (PROVIDER_STALLED / PROVIDER_OUTPUT_INVALID) even though the fix work landed in the tree; the entire fix batch is uncommitted working-tree state; an unrelated Epic 03 spec edit (docs/02-specs/03-thread-views-and-smart-compact/epic.md) also sits uncommitted in the tree and should not ride an Epic 02 closeout commit. The four retained non-blocking findings stand as recorded and do not gate closeout.
result.recommendedNextStep: Run one small follow-up fix batch: extend cascadeTurnDelete to include pairedCounterpartSubject for each deleted member message whose live counterpart lies outside the deleted turn (dedupe against the drop set), add a cross-turn regression test (call in t1, late result in t2 via AC-2.8, delete t2 → t1 call summary cleared and requeued at the next source version, rebuilds outcome 'unknown'), re-run green-verify/verify-all, then commit fix-batch-001 plus this follow-up (excluding the unrelated Epic 03 doc edit) and re-run the reverify pass.
